display.title: Erev Pesach Morning: The Fast of the Firstborn and the Siyum
display.summary_short: A short Yiddish lesson for children on Erev Pesach morning: the fast of the firstborn, a father fasting for a young son, and eating at a siyum in shul.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children. On Erev Pesach morning one wakes up, says Modeh Ani, washes negel vasser, gets dressed, davens and eats breakfast. Erev Pesach is a fast day for every firstborn. The Shulchan Aruch says that a firstborn boy who is still young does not fast; his father fasts in his place. The custom is to find a seudas mitzvah, a meal in honor of a mitzvah, because whoever takes part in one may eat. On Erev Pesach morning people make a siyum in shul when they finish learning a whole tractate of Gemara, and many firstborns come to hear the final words of the Gemara so that they can then eat. The recording ends abruptly at this point.
display.lesson: Firstborns fast on Erev Pesach, and joining a siyum on a tractate of Gemara lets them take part in a seudas mitzvah.

relations.note: Same teaching in 'hg1a' at about 16:50-19:25; that version is fuller (adds why the father may wish to eat), this one is trimmed.
